newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SingTel sees new markets from WTO pact.
newsitem.headline: SingTel sees new markets from WTO pact.

text.p: Singapore Telecommunications Ltd (SingTel) sees new opportunities and lower costs from the recent World Trade Organisation (WTO) pact on telecommunication liberalisation, the Business Times newspaper said on Saturday.
The paper quoted SingTel president and chief executive officer Lee Hsien Yang as saying the liberalisation of telecommunication markets would open up opportunities for the company to invest abroad.

"There will be competition on tariffs and pressure on accounting rates to come down. So far as we are a net outpayer for international account settlements, I think that will be beneficial to us," Lee said.
The newspaper said SingTel's total net settlement payments to other telephone companies totalled Singapore $65 million in 1995.
Lee was also quoted as saying that the impact of the WTO agreement on specific markets was not clear as most governments had put forward very general proposals.

"There are markets today which are extremely closed and which may as a result of this initiative be more open and be available for investments. We have to see the impact of that. We are all trying to read the tea leaves," Lee said.
